Explore Hardmoor
Take a journey into Hardmoor and explore our wonderful rooms and beautiful outdoor surroundings.
“Roots of understanding grow deep when curious minds are nourished in nature”.
Nell Regan Kartychok
Outdoor Woodland Learning
All of our children take part in ‘OWL’: Outdoor Woodland Learning.
It’s hard to believe that within a busy city, children are able to find an early years setting that brings together the most beautiful natural surroundings. Look no further because at Hardmoor, outdoor learning forms the heart of our daily life with activities taking place all year, whatever the weather.
Children explore our vast and secure woodland forest, a beautiful campfire setting where learning takes place about the natural world, a potting greenhouse where children can’t wait to plant and grow seeds, plants and food, among more enriching activities.
Hardmoor is home to two chickens who lay eggs daily that the children collect. Our chickens live in our main playground and say ‘hi’ to the children everyday.
Our OWL provision gives children the very best start in developing some every day skills. Including how to explore woodland safely, to using the natural environment for crafting and den building and how to safely use tools when gardening or planting.
“Play is our brain’s favourite way of learning”.
Our Play Rooms
All of our play rooms are large, light and airy with direct access to the gardens. Our settings provide the most warming welcome for all our children and their families, hosted by our kind and nurturing team.
We have 4 spaces: Kits & Rabbits (babies), Hedgehogs (toddlers) and Foxes (pre-school).

pageCache.text:
Outreach Support & Training
Scroll below to find out more about our support for EYFS settings in the wider community. At the bottom of the page you can complete our short form to enquire about support for your setting.
Our nursery and wider Partnership of schools and nursery settings provide EYFS Outreach Support for settings serving Southampton, Hampshire and the wider UK community who have provision for children aged 3 months to 5 years:
Before you read more, get to know our Partnership and our values:
Support we provide includes:
Advice and strategies tailored to your cohort's needs
Tailored Leadership and management support and training for Managers, Headteachers and Leaders
Coaching & modelling good practice with staff
Support and action plans for enabling environments linked to ITERS & ECERS
Training for teachers and Early Years educators
Guidance on EYFS curriculum adaptations & Literature Reviews
Assessment & tracking needs
Creating observations of the child in the setting
Assessment and tracking systems using a specialised 18-point scale
Pre-phonics training - Rainbow Phase (Pip and Pap Phonics)
Access to a supportive network of practitioners from a range of settings to enhance provision and outcomes
Support with budgeting and finance management
Who delivers the training?
Our Executive Headteacher and leadership team with 20+ years of experience in National Leadership and support across many settings and Local Authorities
Our Director of Teaching & Learning (over 20 years of experience in Primary Education)
Local Authority EYFS Specialist Support Advisor (over 20 years of teaching experience, including Headship)
Our Director of Early Years (18 years teaching experience in Southampton & Hampshire EYFS schools)
Our EYFS Lead Practitioners
Our Outstanding EYFS - Year R Teachers (ECTs - Experienced EYFS Teachers)
Our Outstanding Nursery Teachers (Over 20 years experience working in Nurseries in both PVI and school maintained Nurseries)
Our Early Years Educators (Apprentices, Level 3 Practitioners, NPQEYLs)
Who can access our support?
Testimonials
We are recognised and trusted by Southampton City Council to deliver training support to settings across the city as part of their EYAT programme.
Early Years Advisory Teachers
The Early Years Advisory Teachers (EYATs) and Area SENDCos are part of the Education Standards Service. They offer specialist support to those working within the Early Years Foundation Stage (EYFS) approach. This includes early years settings, as well as colleagues working in Year R and Year 1.
The EYATs are qualified teachers with extensive experience in teaching, curriculum, and leadership within the Foundation Stage. They provide high-quality, tailored support for the EYFS and beyond. They contribute to raising attainment and improving outcomes for children. They also support schools in applying early years principles and approaches with older children. To enhance progress and participation they help to embed:
Developmentally appropriate practice
A focus on engagement and wellbeing
As Area SENDCos, the team also offer support and guidance on delivering the best provision for children with SEND within the Foundation Stage and beyond. This includes guidance on:
Early identification
Staff training to build confidence in meeting a range of needs
Our very own phonics scheme, Pip and Pap Phonics, has a programme specifically curated for EYFS settings.

Learning at Hardmoor
“Our DNA is Messy Play” at Hardmoor and this mantra guides our every day imagination and creative adventures. We ensure there are opportunities for all of our children to learn through storytelling and immersive activities that are curated by our team of Early Years specialists. From the moment children arrive to the moment they leave there is always something special waiting to capture their imagination.

Safeguarding
Scroll below to find out more about our Safeguarding procedures and policies.
Safeguarding is everyone's responsibility.
The policy below details the Safeguarding and Child Protection Procedures we undertake at Hardmoor.
If you think a child is in immediate danger, don't delay - call the police via 999 or the NSPCC via 0808 800 5000 straight away.
Southampton City Council Children’s Services can be contact by calling 02380 83 3004. Out of Hours number - 02380 23 3344.
Lead Designated Safeguarding Lead Officers across the Learning Federation Partnership of Schools:
Gerida Montague, MBE, Sarah Hendricks, Caroline Firman, Jo McNicholas & Paul Lodge
Hardmoor Designated Safeguarding Lead Officers:
Jo McNicholas, Maria Cassar, Melanie Jackson & Room Leads
Our Safeguarding Team will listen to any concerns you have about members of our school community in a confidential manner.
The safety and well being of our children is our highest priority at all times. We have a range of safeguarding measures in place and robust child protection procedures.
As a school we have a responsibility to inform children and family services if we have concerns about the welfare and safety of a child in our school. We ensure the protection of children through:
A SAFE ENVIRONMENT: for children where they can learn and develop
RAISING AWARENESS: give children the knowledge they need to stay safe
ROBUST PROCEDURES: to identify and report suspected abuse
SUPPORTING CHILDREN: in line with their Child Protection Plan in cases of abuse
SAFE RECRUITMENT: based on a system of both DBS and employment checks
For your child’s safety we ask all visitors to ensure they enter through the main entrance to the school and report to a member of the office staff, signing into the visitors’ log and receiving a visitors’ badge if required.
Visitors are asked to leave mobile phones in the admin areas as we are a “mobile free” zone in all bases.
